dedupe_keys.name: seismic detection using submarine cable polarization signals with machine learning

description: Michele Morelli and colleagues publish a machine-learning workflow for detecting earthquakes from submarine-cable polarization signals. Zenodo archives code and data under CC BY 4.0. The description names preprocessing of seismic and state-of-polarization time series, spectral and short-term-average benchmarks, feature-based classifiers, LSTM autoencoders and earthquake-event mapping. Required segmented time-series and feature dataframes are reported as included pickle files. The model can assess whether existing cable infrastructure can contribute to seismic hazard monitoring and can supply events to cable-risk simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this polarization-based detector. Coverage is the cable and earthquake cases in the study, not a general global warning network. A limitation is that classifier performance may depend on cable configuration, traffic noise and labelled event balance, none of which was independently checked. Detection does not by itself estimate cable damage or service loss. The archive was not downloaded, and no detection metric or false-alarm rate was reproduced.
